clue.text: Godfather changes places at a place of worship

indicators.note: the two halves of the clue word swap ends, so the second half moves round to the front

parts.note: a godfather split as GOD plus PA, father

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss swaps seats at a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes places' turns GODPA into PAGOD by moving PA to the front; A comes from the clue's own 'a', and 'at' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Buddhist or Hindu temple tower, a building for worship in East Asia.

clue.text: Support includes one who leads the way

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it, as a container holds its contents

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A supporter brings in someone who blazes the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first person to explore or settle somewhere, opening the way for others.

clue.text: Fellow rides horse from whence came good news

indicators.note: the fellow sits astride the horse, so the horse's letter ends up within the fellow

parts.note: a gent is a man, a fellow
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A man on horseback recalls Browning's galloping messengers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Robert Browning's poem 'How They Brought the Good News from Ghent to Aix', about riders galloping from the Belgian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning's famous poem has horsemen carrying good news out of this Belgian city to Aix.

clue.text: Two-faced without deception, actually

indicators.note: deceiving muddles things up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
read as 'with out': W, the usual short form of with, is taken out

explanation.surface: Someone two-faced finally drops the act and speaks frankly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' splits as 'W out', removing W from TWOFACED to leave TOFACED, which 'deception' rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means existing in fact, whether or not by right, which is to say actually.

clue.text: Dirty looks at ruminant left on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship means being inside it, so the ship's letters go around

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one boards
a cow chews the cud, a ruminant

explanation.surface: Sour glances are thrown at a cow left on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowls are angry frowns, the sort of glowering expressions called dirty looks.

clue.text: Compound where all come dancing

indicators.note: letters that dance jump about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An invitation to a ballroom where everyone is welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the TV show 'Come Dancing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calomel is mercurous chloride, a chemical compound once used as a purgative.

clue.text: When Brock managed support for creative activity

indicators.note: the letters are handled and organised into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A badger called Brock somehow becomes a patron of the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A workbench is a sturdy table that supports a craftsman's making and mending.

clue.text: Sent round one religious and wise

indicators.note: the first word goes around the pieces that follow it

parts.note: taken as written
A is the indefinite article, meaning one
pi is slang for pious, religious

explanation.surface: A devout and sagacious figure is dispatched on a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a literary word for wise or discerning, as in Homo sapiens.

clue.text: There's nothing free with church in bloom

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: the church's letters are placed inside the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: No charge for flowers in the parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, prized for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Price of poor led astray by bargain

parts.note: money is the price one pays
'the price of' something is the money for it

indicators.note: letters that go astray wander out of their order

explanation.surface: The poor are misled into accepting a cheap deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money for old rope' is a British idiom for easy profit from little effort; 'astray' rearranges POORLED.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means gain for almost nothing, a great deal for whoever gets it, hence a bargain.

clue.text: Start of school year about being putrefactive

parts.note: Sept, short for September, when the British school year begins
a being is one, an individual, written I as a numeral
C is short for circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: Something rotten is going on as the autumn term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the school year starts in September. 'being' as I (one) is a loose equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: Septic means infected with bacteria that cause putrefaction, so it is putrefying.

clue.text: Whom beer affected should keep away from it!

definitions.text: Whom beer affected should keep away from it!

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed, as a drinker is by beer, and reordered

explanation.surface: A warning that anyone the worse for drink should stay off the stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue says drinkers who suffer from beer should avoid the drink they make in their own kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Homemade beer is the drink a person affected by beer should avoid, the whole clue describing it.

clue.text: Fish van, say, on Watling Street

parts.note: cray is short for crayfish
Ford makes the Transit van, an example of the make

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's van parked on an old Roman road.
explanation.walkthrough: Crayford is a town in south-east London on Watling Street, the Roman road from Dover through London.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies on the old Roman road, so it is a place situated on that route.

clue.text: After long time orders almanacs

indicators.note: the orders come after the long time, so that word goes second

parts.note: a year is a long period of time
to book is to order or reserve

explanation.surface: After a long wait the reference annuals are ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearbooks are annual publications of facts and figures, much like almanacs.

clue.text: Boy gets it with variable mildness

parts.note: Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard
Y is a common algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A lad takes things easy, gently varying them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenity is gentleness or leniency, especially in punishment, a kind of mildness.

clue.text: Current vicar's beginning to change and update

indicators.note: the vicar's title takes the opening position, ahead of the current

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
amp is short for ampere, the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A new vicar sets out to modernise the parish.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp something is to give it a new look, changing and modernising it.

clue.text: It's important to get out when carrying information

indicators.note: the outer word carries the inner one within it

parts.note: to exit is to get out
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Advice to leave quickly while bearing the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or demanding urgent attention, hence important.

clue.text: Cornish village, being classy, holds archdeacon to be an upstart

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the inner one between them

parts.note: Par is a village in Cornwall
U means upper-class, classy
Ven, short for Venerable, is an archdeacon's title

explanation.surface: A snobbish Cornish village takes in a churchman who has risen too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a person newly risen in wealth or status, regarded as an upstart.

clue.text: Oracle prays without a hope, unfortunately

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is a disordered one, so the letters are rearranged
the letter is removed from the word it follows

explanation.surface: Someone prays without hope, as the oracle foretold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A from PRAYS, leaving PRYS; 'unfortunately' rearranges PRYS plus HOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracle used as a verb means to foretell, which is to prophesy.

clue.text: It's no big deal about Roger being considerable

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the inner letter

parts.note: petty means trivial, no big deal
R is the radio code for roger, received

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off Roger as a substantial matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty can mean fairly large, as in 'a pretty sum', so considerable.

clue.text: Died at the spot, which is disgusting

parts.note: ob is short for obiit, Latin for 'he or she died'
a scene is the place where something happens, the spot

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed on the spot, a revolting sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to decency, which is to say disgusting.

clue.text: Dreamlike county curtailed with a line

indicators.note: having its tail cut off, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Surrey is a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: A county is cut short beside a drawn line.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means bizarre and fantastic, having the strange quality of a dream.

clue.text: Flying gives Robin ear trouble

indicators.note: troubled letters are stirred up and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A robin's ear ailment keeps it aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne means carried through the air, in flight.

clue.text: Sort of entertainment seen as turning weary

indicators.note: the short word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: to weary is to tire

explanation.surface: A show regarded as becoming tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is a genre of comedy mocking folly, a kind of entertainment.

clue.text: Means used by police to produce tears

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into a different word

explanation.surface: Police methods that make people cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun, a device carried by police officers.

clue.text: See over the crash, perhaps, and pick up the remains

indicators.note: signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Witnesses survey the wreck and gather what is left after the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket trophy contested by England and Australia; regaining it means winning back the series.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means gathering up burnt remains, a cryptic take on winning back the trophy.

clue.text: Where there's an even chance to bring back the cat

indicators.note: the word is brought back, reading in reverse

parts.note: puss is a familiar name for the cat

explanation.surface: A gamble on whether to bring the cat home.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is a situation whose outcome is as uncertain as a coin flip.

clue.text: The essence of Sarcozy's movement?

parts.note: in French 'essence' is the word for motor fuel, so the French president's movement runs on it

explanation.surface: A question about the core of the French president's political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarkozy (misspelt in the clue) was President of France; the French for motor fuel is 'essence'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for car fuel is essence, so the essence of a Frenchman's travel is fuel.
